<!--
Feature requests are fine, with a few realities up front:

- The maintenance bar is high. Aerodrome already has plenty of
  surface area; the maintainer is conservative about adding more,
  especially for use cases not personally exercised.
- There is no public roadmap and no committed delivery dates.
  If a request lands in the maintainer's own backlog, you may see
  it in a future release. If it doesn't, it doesn't.
- A "no" isn't an indictment of the idea. It usually means the
  idea is good but not aligned with where the codebase is going.
  That's exactly the case where forking makes sense — the MIT
  license has you covered.

See CONTRIBUTING.md for the longer version.
-->

## What you'd like Aerodrome to do

<!-- A clear description of the feature or change you're suggesting. -->

## Why it matters to you

<!--
Concrete use case from your own ADS-B receiver setup, ideally.
The "I want it for myself" filter applies in reverse here: when
a feature is something the suggester actually uses, the design
discussion is much sharper than abstract framing.
-->

## How it might fit (optional)

<!-- Where in the existing UI or architecture you imagine this living. Skip if you don't have an opinion. -->

## What you've already tried (optional)

<!--
If you've worked around the absence of this feature with a config
tweak, an external script, or something on the receiver side, a
quick note about that helps calibrate how much friction the gap
is causing.
-->
